thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident P-98321 fired: p99 latency SLO burn (service=runtime-api, region=eu-west). Alert threshold crossed: p99 > 1500ms for 5m. https://pagerduty.com/incidents/P-98321 :rotating_light:
pagerduty: PagerDuty link: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/P-98321 — Acknowledgement required
alice: I'm on it, grabbing the bridge. Can someone check whether this is KV-cache related or model slowdowns?
ben: Looking at traces now — lots of long tail on token generation after step 2, not obvious kernel OOM. Metric dump: `p95=420ms p99=1720ms q99.9=4.8s` across EU clusters.
carla: Not seeing obvious GPU queuing. Sidecar latency spiking before the runtime. Could be router/backpressure + a few hot keys.
daniel-sre: Oncall rotation note: I'm the PD ack (rotating). I'll coordinate handoff if needed. First action: mute autopager for this policy to avoid noisy fanout. `incident-bot mute-rule latency-p99-eu 15m`
alice: Done. Autopager suppression in flight — will set to 30m if we get repeated alerts. :white_check_mark:
ben: Quick mitigation idea: temporarily reduce `max_batch_tokens` on the hot pool from 1024 -> 256 to prefer latency over throughput. Pushing config now:```
api call: POST /config/pool/hot -d '{"max_batch_tokens":256}'
Result: accepted (change-id 5d7f)```
carla: Patch applied to 3/4 hot instances, warming now. Watching latency.
alice: Can we fallback affected customer traffic to dedicated capacity in eu-west-dedicated? That would protect SLA customers.
daniel-sre: Routing policy change prepared: `route: latency-failover -> dedicated-eu` will flip for customers in tier=enterprise. Planning a gradual shift (5% -> 50% -> 100%) to avoid thundering herd. Kicking off now.
pagerduty: PagerDuty note: Incident acknowledged by alice at 1747654330. Escalation (level 2) will be used after 12m if no mitigation.
ben: After batch size change and routing partial shift: p95=360ms p99=980ms q99.9=1.6s. Improvement but still above goal for some requests. KV-cache hitrate for the route is low (~12%). Might need cache warm step.
emma-eng: Starting controlled prefix-warm for the busy models: running a set of synthetic prompts for top 200 prefixes. Script: `./tools/warm_prefixes --model redwood-3b --prefix-list top200.txt --rate 10rps`
carla: Warm job started. Also evicting a few old KV entries to rebalance memory on sidecars.
alice: Customer impact: metrics show ~4% of EU requests experienced >2s completion over the past 10m. No mass failures, mostly tail latency for long-context requests. Reached out to solutions for high-touch customers we proactively shift.
daniel-sre: If this stabilizes in 10m we'll close the PD incident and do a postmortem. If not, escalate to platform-eng and consider rolling back last model kernel change (deployed yesterday).
ben: Quick log snippet (filtered):```
[2026-02-14T02:05:12Z] req=ae3ff token_gen=3.7s kernel=0.2s sidecar_queue=1.1s model_step=2.4s
[2026-02-14T02:06:01Z] req=b9c12 token_gen=4.9s kernel=0.3s sidecar_queue=2.0s model_step=2.6s
```
alice: Noted. We're seeing consistent sidecar_queue numbers. Could be batching/regulator hysteresis during burst. Follow-up: add a quick metric alert to detect sidecar_queue>800ms so we can auto-scale the pool earlier.
carla: Agree. I'll open a ticket and a short-runbook item: `runbook: if p99>1500 and sidecar_queue>800ms -> decrease max_batch_tokens, increase pool-target by 1.5x, warm kv prefixes.`
pagerduty: Incident status: status=monitoring (mitigation in progress). Incident updated by alice at 1747654390.
alice: TL;DR: Muted autopager to avoid cascade, decreased batch tokens, partial failover to dedicated capacity, started KV warm. p99 improved from 1720ms -> 980ms. Will monitor next 20m and then perform post-incident debrief. If anyone sees regression, ping @alice direct.
ben: Thanks all. I'll keep an eye on the bridge and metric dashboards.
daniel-sre: Preparing handoff to morning oncall in 25m — will include the runbook note.
emma-eng: Follow-up action: create an eval to catch this regression in perf-ci and add sentinel prefixes to nightly checks.
alice: Closing PD if no further regressions in 20m. Marking for postmortem and owners: eng-runtime (ben), eng-sre (daniel-sre), eng-platform (carla). :clipboard:
